_meta.licence: PokeAPI community data; Pokemon names/flavor are franchise data
_meta.note: Mainline species data only: dex number, genus, Pokedex lore, form list, evolution conditions. Mezastar PE / gimmick / roulette are NOT here.

tags.name: Abomasnow
tags.lore: A powerful Pokémon that can split huge boulders with ease. Dislikes associating with others and chooses to live quietly deep within the mountains, playing with the snow.

tags.name: Abra
tags.lore: Spends 18 hours of the day sleeping. Even while asleep, Abra can control its psychic powers—should danger approach, the Pokémon will simply teleport away.

tags.name: Absol
tags.lore: Because of this Pokémon's ability to detect danger, people mistook Absol as a bringer of doom.

tags.name: Aerodactyl
tags.lore: Aerodactyl's sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.

tags.name: Aggron
tags.lore: Long ago, there was a king who wore a helmet meant to resemble the head of an Aggron. He was trying to channel the Pokémon's strength.

tags.name: Alakazam
tags.lore: The longer Alakazam lives, the larger and heavier its head becomes. Our tests have shown that the strength of its psychic powers correlates positively to the weight of its head.

tags.name: Alcremie
tags.lore: When Alcremie is content, the cream it secretes from its hands becomes sweeter and richer.

tags.name: Alolan Ninetales
tags.lore: The coat of gleaming golden fur is quite magnificent. This species is said to store sacred power in its nine long tails and to live for a millennium.

tags.name: Alolan Sandshrew
tags.lore: It burrows into the ground to create its nest. If hard stones impede its tunneling, it uses its sharp claws to shatter them and then carries on digging.

tags.name: Alolan Sandslash
tags.lore: It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.

tags.name: Alolan Vulpix
tags.lore: In its belly burns a fire, which Vulpix spits out in the form of fireballs. When young, this Pokémon has but one white tail. As the Pokémon matures, this single tail splits into six.

tags.name: Appletun
tags.lore: Its body is covered in sweet nectar, and the skin on its back is especially yummy. Children used to have it as a snack.

tags.name: Arcanine
tags.lore: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

tags.name: Arceus
tags.lore: It is the heavenly fount from which pours the light that shines across Hisui. Its luminance guides and protects all Pokémon. Hisuian mythology states that Arceus is the creator of all things.

tags.name: Arctibax
tags.lore: It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax's strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.

tags.name: Arctovish
tags.lore: The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.

tags.name: Arctozolt
tags.lore: This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.

tags.name: Armarouge
tags.lore: This Pokémon clads itself in armor that has been fortified by psychic and fire energy, and it shoots blazing fireballs.

tags.name: Axew
tags.lore: They play with each other by knocking their large tusks together. Their tusks break sometimes, but they grow back so quickly that it isn't a concern.

tags.name: Baxcalibur
tags.lore: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.

tags.name: Bayleef
tags.lore: Bayleef's neck is ringed by curled-up leaves. Inside each tubular leaf is a small shoot of a tree. The fragrance of this shoot makes people peppy.

tags.name: Beldum
tags.lore: The cells in this Pokémon's body are composed of magnetic material. Instead of blood, magnetic forces flow through Beldum's body.

tags.name: Blastoise
tags.lore: The rocket cannons on its shell fire jets of water capable of punching holes through thick steel.

tags.name: Blaziken
tags.lore: Blaziken has incredibly strong legs—it can easily clear a 30-story building in one leap. This Pokémon's blazing punches leave its foes scorched and blackened.

tags.name: Blipbug
tags.lore: Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.

tags.name: Boltund
tags.lore: It sends electricity through its legs to boost their strength. Running at top speed, it easily breaks 50 mph.

tags.name: Bronzong
tags.lore: Some believe that its bell-like cry opens holes to another world. It has been revered as a deity since ancient times.

tags.name: Bronzor
tags.lore: Floats using a mysterious energy. The pattern engraved upon its back is held as sacred and can sometimes be found in imagery from ancient cemeteries and other such timeworn places.

tags.name: Budew
tags.lore: When the sun's light strengthens, the bud atop this Pokémon's head opens. This is a sign to the people that the harsh winter is over, and the season of budding has begun.

tags.name: Calyrex
tags.lore: Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.

tags.name: Carkol
tags.lore: By rapidly rolling its legs, it can travel at over 18 mph. The temperature of the flames it breathes exceeds 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit.

tags.name: Ceruledge
tags.lore: An old set of armor steeped in grudges caused this Pokémon's evolution. Ceruledge cuts its enemies to pieces without mercy.

tags.name: Chandelure
tags.lore: In homes illuminated by Chandelure instead of lights, funerals were a constant occurrence— or so it's said.

tags.name: Charcadet
tags.lore: Its firepower increases when it fights, reaching over 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. It likes berries that are rich in fat.

tags.name: Charizard
tags.lore: Its wings can carry this Pokémon close to an altitude of 4,600 feet. It blows out fire at very high temperatures.

tags.name: Charjabug
tags.lore: Its digestive processes convert the leaves it eats into electricity. An electric sac in its belly stores the electricity for later use.

tags.name: Chikorita
tags.lore: In battle, Chikorita waves its leaf around to keep the foe at bay. However, a sweet fragrance also wafts from the leaf, becalming the battling Pokémon and creating a cozy, friendly atmosphere all around.

tags.name: Chimchar
tags.lore: Full of vigor and always in high spirits. It was once known by the name ”Lantern-Tail” and feared as some kind of apparition.

tags.name: Cinderace
tags.lore: It's skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.

tags.name: Coalossal
tags.lore: While it's engaged in battle, its mountain of coal will burn bright red, sending off sparks that scorch the surrounding area.

tags.name: Combusken
tags.lore: Combusken battles with the intensely hot flames it spews from its beak and with outstandingly destructive kicks. This Pokémon's cry is very loud and distracting.

tags.name: Copperajah
tags.lore: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.

tags.name: Corviknight
tags.lore: With their great intellect and flying skills, these Pokémon very successfully act as the Galar region's airborne taxi service.

tags.name: Cradily
tags.lore: Once Cradily catches prey in its tentacles, it digests them whole and absorbs their nutrients.

tags.name: Cramorant
tags.lore: This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.

tags.name: Crocalor
tags.lore: The valve in Crocalor's flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way.

tags.name: Croconaw
tags.lore: Once Croconaw has clamped its jaws on its foe, it will absolutely not let go. Because the tips of its fangs are forked back like barbed fishhooks, they become impossible to remove when they have sunk in.

tags.name: Cyndaquil
tags.lore: Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.

tags.name: Dedenne
tags.lore: Since Dedenne can't generate much electricity on its own, it steals electricity from outlets or other electric Pokémon.

tags.name: Deino
tags.lore: Because it can't see, this Pokémon is constantly biting at everything it touches, trying to keep track of its surroundings.

tags.name: Dewott
tags.lore: Its exquisite double-scalchop technique is likely the result of daily training, and it can send even masters of the blade fleeing in defeat.

tags.name: Dialga
tags.lore: This Pokémon is revered as a deity in Hisuian legend. The birth of Dialga was what caused the vast river of time to begin flowing in our world.

tags.name: Dodrio
tags.lore: One of Doduo's two heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 mph in prairies.

tags.name: Doduo
tags.lore: Its short wings make flying difficult. Instead, this Pokémon runs at high speed on developed legs.

tags.name: Dottler
tags.lore: As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.

tags.name: Dracovish
tags.lore: Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can't breathe unless it's underwater.

tags.name: Dracozolt
tags.lore: The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.

tags.name: Dragapult
tags.lore: Apparently the Dreepy inside Dragapult's horns eagerly look forward to being launched out at Mach speeds.

tags.name: Drakloak
tags.lore: Without a Dreepy to place on its head and care for, it gets so uneasy it'll try to substitute any Pokémon it finds for the missing Dreepy.

tags.name: Drampa
tags.lore: Drampa is a kind and friendly Pokémon—up until it's angered. When that happens, it stirs up a gale and flattens everything around.

tags.name: Drednaw
tags.lore: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.

tags.name: Dreepy
tags.lore: If this weak Pokémon is by itself, a mere child could defeat it. But if Dreepy has friends to help it train, it can evolve and become much stronger.

tags.name: Drifblim
tags.lore: It drifts along at dusk, perfectly silent. Its transient, melancholy aspect touches some people deeply—every so often, one will come upon a song or poem devoted to Drifblim.

tags.name: Drifloon
tags.lore: Said to lure away young children and carry them off to the afterlife. Some whisper that Drifloon are formed of reincarnated human souls, but these rumors are as yet unconfirmed.

tags.name: Drilbur
tags.lore: It's a digger, using its claws to burrow through the ground. It causes damage to vegetable crops, so many farmers have little love for it.

tags.name: Drizzile
tags.lore: Highly intelligent but also very lazy, it keeps enemies out of its territory by laying traps everywhere.

tags.name: Dubwool
tags.lore: Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.

tags.name: Duraludon
tags.lore: The special metal that composes its body is very light, so this Pokémon has considerable agility. It lives in caves because it dislikes the rain.

tags.name: Dusclops
tags.lore: There are rumors that peeking inside its bandage-wrapped body will cause one to get pulled in through the gaps between the bandages, never to return. I've been too scared to verify.

tags.name: Dusknoir
tags.lore: Comes to those whose lives have come to an end and escorts their souls to the afterlife. Known to mistakenly take the souls of those who yet have life left in them, albeit rarely.

tags.name: Duskull
tags.lore: I've heard that the children of Hisui all begin to behave once they've been told the story of how this Pokémon roams about before the witching hour to spirit away misbehaving children.

tags.name: Eelektrik
tags.lore: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

tags.name: Eelektross
tags.lore: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

tags.name: Eevee
tags.lore: Harbors the potential to evolve into manifold forms. Within Eevee lies the key to the mysteries of Pokémon evolution—I'm certain of it.

tags.name: Eldegoss
tags.lore: The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.

tags.name: Electabuzz
tags.lore: Feeds on electrical energy. During sudden showers beneath looming thunderclouds, one can observe Electabuzz scaling tall trees, where the Pokémon will then wait for lightning to strike.

tags.name: Electivire
tags.lore: Its evolution was induced by an unusual item, and its electrical output rises along with its heart rate. From its tails, it can unleash an electric current measuring 20,000 volts.

tags.name: Elekid
tags.lore: They generate electricity by spinning their arms. During a thunderstorm, if one hears the lively voices of children out in the wilderness, what one is actually hearing are the voices of Elekid.

tags.name: Emboar
tags.lore: It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.

tags.name: Empoleon
tags.lore: Since ancient times, it has been revered by the people of Hisui, who call it the Master of the Waves. Its wings are a match for even master-crafted blades.

tags.name: Entei
tags.lore: Entei embodies the passion of magma. This Pokémon is thought to have been born in the eruption of a volcano. It sends up massive bursts of fire that utterly consume all that they touch.

tags.name: Espeon
tags.lore: Wields an arcane power with which it can predict the weather and even people's thoughts. When bathed in sunshine, the scarlet orb on its brow glows and builds energy.

tags.name: Eternatus
tags.lore: It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.

tags.name: Excadrill
tags.lore: Known as the Drill King, this Pokémon can tunnel through the terrain at speeds of over 90 mph.

tags.name: Feebas
tags.lore: It is a shabby and ugly Pokémon. However, it is very hardy and can survive on little water.

tags.name: Feraligatr
tags.lore: Feraligatr intimidates its foes by opening its huge mouth. In battle, it will kick the ground hard with its thick and powerful hind legs to charge at the foe at an incredible speed.

tags.name: Flapple
tags.lore: It flies on wings of apple skin and spits a powerful acid. It can also change its shape into that of an apple.

tags.name: Flareon
tags.lore: Flames burn within a saclike organ inside this Pokémon. When Flareon inhales, these flames grow in intensity, reaching a mighty 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

tags.name: Fletchinder
tags.lore: Fletchinder are exceedingly territorial and aggressive. These Pokémon fight among themselves over feeding grounds.

tags.name: Fletchling
tags.lore: When this Pokémon gets excited, its body temperature increases sharply. If you touch a Fletchling with bare hands, you might get burned.

tags.name: Floragato
tags.lore: The hardness of Floragato's fur depends on the Pokémon's mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp.

tags.name: Flygon
tags.lore: It is nicknamed the Desert Spirit because the flapping of its wings sounds like a woman singing.

tags.name: Fraxure
tags.lore: Its skin is as hard as a suit of armor. Fraxure's favorite strategy is to tackle its opponents, stabbing them with its tusks at the same time.

tags.name: Frigibax
tags.lore: This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.

tags.name: Frosmoth
tags.lore: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.

tags.name: Fuecoco
tags.lore: Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco's head and flickers to and fro.

tags.name: Galarian Farfetch'd
tags.lore: They use a plant stalk as a weapon, but not all of them use it in the same way. Several distinct styles of stalk fighting have been observed.

tags.name: Galarian Linoone
tags.lore: It uses its explosive speed and razor-sharp claws to bring down prey. Running along winding paths is not its strong suit.

tags.name: Galarian Meowth
tags.lore: It washes its face regularly to keep the coin on its forehead spotless. It doesn't get along with Galarian Meowth.

tags.name: Galarian Weezing
tags.lore: It can't suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.

tags.name: Galarian Zigzagoon
tags.lore: Zigzagoon that adapted to regions outside Galar acquired this appearance. If you've lost something, this Pokémon can likely find it.

tags.name: Gallade
tags.lore: The blades extending from its elbows are sharper than the finest swords. Its swordsmanship, albeit self-taught, is astonishingly impressive.

tags.name: Gardevoir
tags.lore: It will dedicate itself to defending a master it has come to adore. Its pure white dress, reminiscent of those worn by ladies of nobility, is the dress of one who is willing to risk their life.

tags.name: Gengar
tags.lore: Possesses potential victims' shadows in an effort to steal away the victims' lives. If your shadow begins to laugh, you must take hold of a protective charm posthaste!

tags.name: Glaceon
tags.lore: Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.

tags.name: Golett
tags.lore: This Pokémon was created from clay. It received orders from its master many thousands of years ago, and it still follows those orders to this day.

tags.name: Golisopod
tags.lore: They live in sunken ships or in holes in the seabed. When Golisopod and Grapploct battle, the loser becomes the winner's meal.

tags.name: Golurk
tags.lore: There's a theory that inside Golurk is a perpetual motion machine that produces limitless energy, but this belief hasn't been proven.

tags.name: Goodra
tags.lore: Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.

tags.name: Gossifleur
tags.lore: It whirls around in the wind while singing a joyous song. This delightful display has charmed many into raising this Pokémon.

tags.name: Great Tusk
tags.lore: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.

tags.name: Greedent
tags.lore: Common throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon has strong teeth and can chew through the toughest of berry shells.

tags.name: Greninja
tags.lore: It appears and vanishes with a ninja's grace. It toys with its enemies using swift movements, while slicing them with throwing stars of sharpest water.

tags.name: Grimmsnarl
tags.lore: Its hairs work like muscle fibers. When its hairs unfurl, they latch on to opponents, ensnaring them as tentacles would.

tags.name: Grookey
tags.lore: It attacks with rapid beats of its stick. As it strikes with amazing speed, it gets more and more pumped.

tags.name: Grotle
tags.lore: Appears where there is clean spring water. The fruit that grows on the shrubs on its shell is sweet, nutritious, and truly delicious.

tags.name: Groudon
tags.lore: Through Primal Reversion and with nature's full power, it will take back its true form. It can cause magma to erupt and expand the landmass of the world.

tags.name: Grovyle
tags.lore: This Pokémon adeptly flies from branch to branch in trees. In a forest, no Pokémon can ever hope to catch a fleeing Grovyle however fast they may be.

tags.name: Growlithe
tags.lore: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

tags.name: Grubbin
tags.lore: It uses its big jaws to dig nests into the forest floor, and it loves to feed on sweet tree sap.

tags.name: Hatenna
tags.lore: If this Pokémon senses a strong emotion, it will run away as fast as it can. It prefers areas without people.

tags.name: Hatterene
tags.lore: If you're too loud around it, you risk being torn apart by the claws on its tentacle. This Pokémon is also known as the Forest Witch.

tags.name: Hattrem
tags.lore: Using the braids on its head, it pummels foes to get them to quiet down. One blow from those braids would knock out a professional boxer.

tags.name: Haxorus
tags.lore: While usually kindhearted, it can be terrifying if angered. Tusks that can slice through steel beams are how Haxorus deals with its adversaries.

tags.name: Heracross
tags.lore: This Pokémon has an unparalleled horn. Heracross itself demonstrates tremendous power—it's capable of throwing several people trained in the traditional arts of war at once.

tags.name: Hisuian Zoroark
tags.lore: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark's own body.

tags.name: Hisuian Zorua
tags.lore: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.

tags.name: Ho-Oh
tags.lore: Ho-Oh's feathers glow in seven colors depending on the angle at which they are struck by light. These feathers are said to bring happiness to the bearers. This Pokémon is said to live at the foot of a rainbow.

tags.name: Honchkrow
tags.lore: One cry from this Pokémon, and a murder of Murkrow come flying. At such times, one would think the curtain of night had fallen, plunging the world into jet-black darkness.

tags.name: Hydreigon
tags.lore: The three heads take turns sinking their teeth into the opponent. Their attacks won't slow until their target goes down.

tags.name: Impidimp
tags.lore: It sneaks into people's homes, stealing things and feasting on the negative energy of the frustrated occupants.

tags.name: Infernape
tags.lore: A tall, hardy Pokémon with a dazzling appearance. It shrouds itself in flame and battles as if engaged in dance—truly a sight to behold.

tags.name: Inteleon
tags.lore: Its nictitating membranes let it pick out foes' weak points so it can precisely blast them with water that shoots from its fingertips at Mach 3.

tags.name: Iron Treads
tags.lore: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

tags.name: Jolteon
tags.lore: Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.

tags.name: Jynx
tags.lore: The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.

tags.name: Kadabra
tags.lore: There are rumors that a child with mystical powers became a Kadabra; however, this remains unverified. I suspect that the spoon Kadabra holds enhances its brain waves.

tags.name: Keldeo
tags.lore: They say that Keldeo must survive harsh battles and fully develop the horn on its forehead before this Pokémon's true power will awaken.

tags.name: Kirlia
tags.lore: It resembles a maiden in appearance, but it wields strange powers to project visions of paradise. I suspect the crimson ornaments on its head are the key to its abilities.

tags.name: Koffing
tags.lore: It adores polluted air. Some claim that Koffing used to be more plentiful in the Galar region than they are now.

tags.name: Kommo-o
tags.lore: Certain ruins have paintings of ancient warriors wearing armor made of Kommo-o scales.

tags.name: Koraidon
tags.lore: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.

tags.name: Kyogre
tags.lore: Kyogre is said to be the personification of the sea itself. Legends tell of its many clashes against Groudon, as each sought to gain the power of nature.

tags.name: Kyurem
tags.lore: It appears that this Pokémon uses its powers over ice to freeze its own body in order to stabilize its cellular structure.

tags.name: Latias
tags.lore: Latias is highly intelligent and capable of understanding human speech. It is covered with a glass-like down. The Pokémon enfolds its body with its down and refracts light to alter its appearance.

tags.name: Latios
tags.lore: Latios will only open its heart to a Trainer with a compassionate spirit. This Pokémon can fly faster than a jet plane by folding its forelegs to minimize air resistance.

tags.name: Leafeon
tags.lore: Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.

tags.name: Lileep
tags.lore: Lileep clings to rocks on the seabed. When prey comes close, this Pokémon entangles it with petallike tentacles.

tags.name: Lucario
tags.lore: A most gallant-looking creature. It emits energy waves and controls them with precision, using them to sense even faraway beings. I have given the name ”aura” to this power.

tags.name: Lugia
tags.lore: Lugia's wings pack devastating power—a light fluttering of its wings can blow apart regular houses. As a result, this Pokémon chooses to live out of sight deep under the sea.

tags.name: Lunala
tags.lore: It steals the light from its surroundings and then becomes the full moon, showering its own light across the night sky.

tags.name: Luxio
tags.lore: Proudly uses its electrified claws as weapons. It seems to be a gracious Pokémon, evenly sharing the spoils of the hunt with others of its kind.

tags.name: Luxray
tags.lore: They form packs, each having one male as leader. Legends say that when Luxray's two eyes shimmer with gold, the Pokémon can see through anything.

tags.name: Machamp
tags.lore: In close combat, its four arms afford it offensive and defensive supremacy. In but a blink, this valiant Pokémon can overwhelm its foes with more than 1,000 blows from its fists.

tags.name: Machoke
tags.lore: A sturdy creature boasting a robust physique and boundless stamina. Loves training above all else and voluntarily assists with tasks such as construction and clearing land.

tags.name: Machop
tags.lore: Though as small as a child, it has strength enough to easily throw a well-built adult. Striving to become ever stronger, Machop trains by carrying a Graveler on its shoulders.

tags.name: Magby
tags.lore: This Pokémon lives in volcanic areas. With each breath, sparks spurt from its mouth and nose. When Magby is in good health, its flames gain a yellow tint.

tags.name: Magmar
tags.lore: Legend has it that this Pokémon was born from the crater of a volcano. When wounded, it bathes in lava to heal its body, much as one would soak in a hot spring.

tags.name: Magmortar
tags.lore: Use of a strange item caused this Pokémon to evolve. Fireballs launched from the ends of its tubelike arms are hot enough to melt an iron pot in an instant.

tags.name: Mamoswine
tags.lore: This species reached its zenith during the period known as the ice age. I suspect that Hisui's frigid climate is in harmony with Mamoswine's constitution, thus awakening hidden potential.

tags.name: Mareanie
tags.lore: Unlike their Alolan counterparts, the Mareanie of the Galar region have not yet figured out that the branches of Corsola are delicious.

tags.name: Marshtomp
tags.lore: Marshtomp is much faster at traveling through mud than it is at swimming. This Pokémon's hindquarters exhibit obvious development, giving it the ability to walk on just its hind legs.

tags.name: Meganium
tags.lore: The fragrance of Meganium's flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe's fighting spirit.

tags.name: Meowscarada
tags.lore: With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what's going on.

tags.name: Metagross
tags.lore: Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.

tags.name: Metang
tags.lore: Using magnetic forces to stay aloft, this Pokémon flies at high speeds, weaving through harsh mountain terrain in pursuit of prey.

tags.name: Mew
tags.lore: When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon's short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.

tags.name: Mewtwo
tags.lore: Its DNA is almost the same as Mew's. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.

tags.name: Milcery
tags.lore: They say that any patisserie visited by Milcery is guaranteed success and good fortune.

tags.name: Milotic
tags.lore: It's said that a glimpse of a Milotic and its beauty will calm any hostile emotions you're feeling.

tags.name: Mimikyu
tags.lore: There was a scientist who peeked under Mimikyu's old rag in the name of research. The scientist died of a mysterious disease.

tags.name: Miraidon
tags.lore: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

tags.name: Monferno
tags.lore: The deeper the blue on its face, the more powerful it will grow to become. It leaps about every which way and lands powerful blows against its opponents with the flame on its tail.

tags.name: Morgrem
tags.lore: With sly cunning, it tries to lure people into the woods. Some believe it to have the power to make crops grow.

tags.name: Mudbray
tags.lore: It eats dirt to create mud and smears this mud all over its feet, giving them the grip needed to walk on rough terrain without slipping.

tags.name: Mudkip
tags.lore: In water, Mudkip breathes using the gills on its cheeks. If it is faced with a tight situation in battle, this Pokémon will unleash its amazing power—it can crush rocks bigger than itself.

tags.name: Mudsdale
tags.lore: Mudsdale has so much stamina that it could carry over 10 tons across the Galar region without rest or sleep.

tags.name: Murkrow
tags.lore: Widely shunned as a bearer of ill fortune. Upon crossing paths with this creature, I've been told one must chant ”Workrum, Workrum—bad luck, don't come” as a protective incantation.

tags.name: Naganadel
tags.lore: One kind of Ultra Beast, it fires a glowing, venomous liquid from its needles. This liquid is also immensely adhesive.

tags.name: Nickit
tags.lore: Cunning and cautious, this Pokémon survives by stealing food from others. It erases its tracks with swipes of its tail as it makes off with its plunder.

tags.name: Nidoking
tags.lore: Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It's forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.

tags.name: Nidoqueen
tags.lore: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.

tags.name: Nidoran♀
tags.lore: It uses its hard incisor teeth to crush and eat berries. The tip of a female Nidoran's horn is a bit more rounded than the tip of a male's horn.

tags.name: Nidoran♂
tags.lore: Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it's friendly with.

tags.name: Nidorina
tags.lore: If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.

tags.name: Nidorino
tags.lore: It's nervous and quick to act aggressively. The potency of its poison increases along with the level of adrenaline present in its body.

tags.name: Noibat
tags.lore: No wavelength of sound is beyond Noibat's ability to produce. The ultrasonic waves it generates can overcome much larger Pokémon.

tags.name: Noivern
tags.lore: Flying through the darkness, it weakens enemies with ultrasonic waves that could crush stone. Its fangs finish the fight.

tags.name: Obstagoon
tags.lore: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

tags.name: Onix
tags.lore: This chain of immense stones resembles a giant serpent. Tremors shake the earth above as it burrows deep beneath the ground, feeding on boulders as it goes.

tags.name: Orbeetle
tags.lore: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what's around it—and what's around it can include things over six miles away.

tags.name: Oshawott
tags.lore: This Pokémon from the Unova region uses the shell on its belly as a weapon to cut down its foes. Thus, I've conferred upon this shell the name ”scalchop”.

tags.name: Palkia
tags.lore: This Pokémon is feared as a deity in Hisuian legend. The birth of Palkia was what caused the walls of our world to disappear, creating a sky that spans for infinity.

tags.name: Pawmi
tags.lore: The pads of its paws are electricity-discharging organs. Pawmi fires electricity from its forepaws while standing unsteadily on its hind legs.

tags.name: Pawmo
tags.lore: Pawmo uses a unique fighting technique in which it uses its forepaws to strike foes and zap them with electricity from its paw pads simultaneously.

tags.name: Pelipper
tags.lore: Skimming the water's surface, it dips its large bill in the sea, scoops up food and water, and carries it.

tags.name: Perrserker
tags.lore: After many battles, it evolved dangerous claws that come together to form daggers when extended.

tags.name: Pidgeot
tags.lore: This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.

tags.name: Pidgeotto
tags.lore: This Pokémon is full of vitality. It constantly flies around its large territory in search of prey.

tags.name: Pidgey
tags.lore: Very docile. If attacked, it will often kick up sand to protect itself rather than fight back.

tags.name: Pignite
tags.lore: When its internal fire flares up, its movements grow sharper and faster. When in trouble, it emits smoke.

tags.name: Pikachu
tags.lore: Possesses cheek sacs in which it stores electricity. This clever forest-dweller roasts tough berries with an electric shock before consuming them.

tags.name: Piloswine
tags.lore: The long fur of this Pokémon covers its eyes, ears, and even limbs, allowing Piloswine to resist harshly frigid conditions. The Pokémon's white tusks can be used to defeat its enemies.

tags.name: Pinsir
tags.lore: This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.

tags.name: Piplup
tags.lore: Prefers cold climes and appears along coasts. It's an adorable little thing—as cute as any child—but it's also prideful, unwilling to accept handouts from people.

tags.name: Poipole
tags.lore: An Ultra Beast that lives in a different world, it cackles wildly as it sprays its opponents with poison from the needles on its head.

tags.name: Poliwag
tags.lore: In rivers with fast-flowing water, this Pokémon will cling to a rock by using its thick lips, which act like a suction cup.

tags.name: Poliwhirl
tags.lore: This Pokémon's sweat is a slimy mucus. When captured, Poliwhirl can slither from its enemies' grasp and escape.

tags.name: Poliwrath
tags.lore: Poliwrath is skilled at both swimming and martial arts. It uses its well-trained arms to dish out powerful punches.

tags.name: Polteageist
tags.lore: Leaving leftover black tea unattended is asking for this Pokémon to come along and pour itself into it, turning the tea into a new Polteageist.

tags.name: Prinplup
tags.lore: It swims gracefully through the frigid sea and sings with a voice like the roaring tide. It has powerful, sturdy wings and dignity to match.

tags.name: Quaquaval
tags.lore: Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes.

tags.name: Quaxly
tags.lore: Its strong legs let it easily swim around in even fast-flowing rivers. It likes to keep things tidy and is prone to overthinking things.

tags.name: Quaxwell
tags.lore: The hardworking Quaxwell observes people and Pokémon from various regions and incorporates their movements into its own dance routines.

tags.name: Quilava
tags.lore: This creature's fur is most mysterious—it is wholly impervious to the burning touch of flame. Should Quilava turn its back to you, take heed! Such a posture indicates a forthcoming attack.

tags.name: Raboot
tags.lore: It kicks berries right off the branches of trees and then juggles them with its feet, practicing its footwork.

tags.name: Raichu
tags.lore: It can discharge bursts of electricity exceeding 100,000 volts— a single strike with that amount of power would incapacitate one of the Copperajah of my homeland.

tags.name: Raikou
tags.lore: Raikou embodies the speed of lightning. The roars of this Pokémon send shock waves shuddering through the air and shake the ground as if lightning bolts had come crashing down.

tags.name: Ralts
tags.lore: Tends to prefer people with a chipper disposition to those who are gloomy, but it has shown no discrimination with regard to age or gender. Needs more research.

tags.name: Rayquaza
tags.lore: It flies forever through the ozone layer, consuming meteoroids for sustenance. The many meteoroids in its body provide the energy it needs to Mega Evolve.

tags.name: Regice
tags.lore: This Pokémon's body is made of solid ice. It's said that Regice was born beneath thick ice in the ice age.

tags.name: Regidrago
tags.lore: Its body is composed of crystallized dragon energy. Regidrago is said to have the powers of every dragon Pokémon.

tags.name: Regieleki
tags.lore: Its entire body is made up of a single organ that generates electrical energy. Regieleki is capable of creating all Galar's electricity.

tags.name: Regirock
tags.lore: Cutting-edge technology was used to study the internals of this Pokémon's rock body, but nothing was found—not even a brain or a heart.

tags.name: Registeel
tags.lore: It's rumored that this Pokémon was born deep underground in the planet's mantle and that it emerged onto the surface 10,000 years ago.

tags.name: Reshiram
tags.lore: According to myth, if people ignore truth and let themselves become consumed by greed, Reshiram will arrive to burn their kingdoms down.

tags.name: Rhyperior
tags.lore: This Pokémon evolved through use of a curious item. Its rocklike hide is composed of a mysterious substance and can withstand a blow from a masterwork sword with nary a scratch.

tags.name: Rillaboom
tags.lore: The one with the best drumming techniques becomes the boss of the troop. It has a gentle disposition and values harmony among its group.

tags.name: Rolycoly
tags.lore: It can race around like a unicycle, even on rough, rocky terrain. Burning coal sustains it.

tags.name: Roselia
tags.lore: Though beautiful, it has highly poisonous thorns. There is an old tradition in my homeland wherein one would send these thorns to an opponent to challenge them to a duel.

tags.name: Roserade
tags.lore: Hidden within the bouquet on each hand are thorned whips loaded with virulent poison. Roserade moves gracefully as it corners its prey and mercilessly lashes them with its whips.

tags.name: Runerigus
tags.lore: Never touch its shadowlike body, or you'll be shown the horrific memories behind the picture carved into it.

tags.name: Samurott
tags.lore: Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon's evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.

tags.name: Sandaconda
tags.lore: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.

tags.name: Sceptile
tags.lore: Sceptile has seeds growing on its back. They are said to be bursting with nutrients that revitalize trees. This Pokémon raises the trees in a forest with loving care.

tags.name: Scolipede
tags.lore: Scolipede engage in fierce territorial battles with Centiskorch. At the end of one of these battles, the victor makes a meal of the loser.

tags.name: Scorbunny
tags.lore: It has special pads on the backs of its feet, and one on its nose. Once it's raring to fight, these pads radiate tremendous heat.

tags.name: Sealeo
tags.lore: Its white whiskers are very sensitive. Sealeo will balance Spheal on the tip of its nose, checking its scent and its feel to be sure the Spheal is healthy.

tags.name: Serperior
tags.lore: It can stop its opponents' movements with just a glare. It takes in solar energy and boosts it internally.

tags.name: Servine
tags.lore: When it gets dirty, its leaves can't be used in photosynthesis, so it always keeps itself clean.

tags.name: Shinx
tags.lore: Shakes its body to generate electricity. Its stature belies its aggression—one must be patient to tame this Pokémon.

tags.name: Silicobra
tags.lore: It spews sand from its nostrils. While the enemy is blinded, it burrows into the ground to hide.

tags.name: Sinistea
tags.lore: The teacup in which this Pokémon makes its home is a famous piece of antique tableware. Many forgeries are in circulation.

tags.name: Sirfetch'd
tags.lore: After deflecting attacks with its hard leaf shield, it strikes back with its sharp leek stalk. The leek stalk is both weapon and food.

tags.name: Skeledirge
tags.lore: Skeledirge's gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.

tags.name: Skwovet
tags.lore: It eats berries nonstop—a habit that has made it more resilient than it looks. It'll show up on farms, searching for yet more berries.

tags.name: Slowbro
tags.lore: Being bitten by a Shellder shocked this Pokémon into standing on two legs. If the Shellder lets go, it seems Slowbro will turn back into a Slowpoke.

tags.name: Slowpoke
tags.lore: When this Pokémon's tail is soaked in water, sweetness seeps from it. Slowpoke uses this trait to lure in and fish up other Pokémon.

tags.name: Sneasel
tags.lore: Its sturdy, curved claws are ideal for traversing precipitous cliffs. From the tips of these claws drips a venom that infiltrates the nerves of any prey caught in Sneasel's grasp.

tags.name: Snivy
tags.lore: They photosynthesize by bathing their tails in sunlight. When they are not feeling well, their tails droop.

tags.name: Snom
tags.lore: It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.

tags.name: Snorlax
tags.lore: This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.

tags.name: Snover
tags.lore: One is likely to encounter this Pokémon while out in the snow. There are stories of Snover appearing in human settlements but doing no harm—rather, they bond with the children.

tags.name: Sobble
tags.lore: When it gets wet, its skin changes color, and this Pokémon becomes invisible as if it were camouflaged.

tags.name: Solgaleo
tags.lore: Solgaleo was once known as the Beast That Devours the Sun. Energy in the form of light radiates boundlessly from it.

tags.name: Spheal
tags.lore: During the season when drift ice approaches the shore, Spheal prefers living on the ice—where fewer predators lurk—rather than the land. Its fur retains heat superbly and resists harsh cold.

tags.name: Sprigatito
tags.lore: The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun.

tags.name: Suicune
tags.lore: Suicune embodies the compassion of a pure spring of water. It runs across the land with gracefulness. This Pokémon has the power to purify dirty water.

tags.name: Swampert
tags.lore: Swampert predicts storms by sensing subtle differences in the sounds of waves and tidal winds with its fins. If a storm is approaching, it piles up boulders to protect itself.

tags.name: Swinub
tags.lore: Swinub excels at sniffing out mushrooms buried beneath grass or snow. Since ancient times, the people of Hisui have often relied upon this skill.

tags.name: Swoobat
tags.lore: The auspicious shape of this Pokémon's nose apparently led some regions to consider Swoobat a symbol of good luck.

tags.name: Sylveon
tags.lore: It emits a soothing aura from its ribbon-shaped organs. It wraps these appendages around quarrelers to instantly restore calm to the situation.

tags.name: Talonflame
tags.lore: Talonflame dives toward prey at speeds of up to 310 mph and assaults them with powerful kicks, giving the prey no chance to escape.

tags.name: Tepig
tags.lore: It loves to eat roasted berries, but sometimes it gets too excited and burns them to a crisp.

tags.name: Thievul
tags.lore: With a lithe body and sharp claws, it goes around stealing food and eggs. Boltund is its natural enemy.

tags.name: Thwackey
tags.lore: When it's drumming out rapid beats in battle, it gets so caught up in the rhythm that it won't even notice that it's already knocked out its opponent.

tags.name: Togedemaru
tags.lore: When it's in trouble, it curls up into a ball, makes its fur spikes stand on end, and then discharges electricity indiscriminately.

tags.name: Torchic
tags.lore: Torchic has a place inside its body where it keeps its flame. Give it a hug—it will be glowing with warmth. This Pokémon is covered all over by a fluffy coat of down.

tags.name: Torterra
tags.lore: This remarkable, large-bodied Pokémon would serve beautifully as borrowed scenery for a garden, and its strength is peerless. Torterra roams the wilderness in search of clean water.

tags.name: Totodile
tags.lore: Despite the smallness of its body, Totodile's jaws are very powerful. While the Pokémon may think it is just playfully nipping, its bite has enough power to cause serious injury.

tags.name: Toxel
tags.lore: It manipulates the chemical makeup of its poison to produce electricity. The voltage is weak, but it can cause a tingling paralysis.

tags.name: Toxtricity
tags.lore: This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.

tags.name: Trapinch
tags.lore: It makes an inescapable conical pit and lies in wait at the bottom for prey to come tumbling down.

tags.name: Treecko
tags.lore: Treecko is cool, calm, and collected—it never panics under any situation. If a bigger foe were to glare at this Pokémon, it would glare right back without conceding an inch of ground.

tags.name: Turtonator
tags.lore: Eating sulfur in its volcanic habitat is what causes explosive compounds to develop in its shell. Its droppings are also dangerously explosive.

tags.name: Turtwig
tags.lore: This Pokémon becomes more energetic the more sunlight there is. The part resembling a shell is similar to silt and is slightly damp and warm to the touch.

tags.name: Tynamo
tags.lore: One alone can emit only a trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.

tags.name: Typhlosion
tags.lore: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.

tags.name: Tyranitar
tags.lore: The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.

tags.name: Umbreon
tags.lore: It is most active in the wee hours of the night, when moonlight bathes the land. Its large eyes can pierce the darkness and perceive prey with absolute clarity.

tags.name: Vaporeon
tags.lore: Tests show that its cells closely resemble water molecules, which perhaps explains its ability to conceal its form while submerged. I believe the origins of mermaid folklore lie with this Pokémon.

tags.name: Venipede
tags.lore: Its fangs are highly venomous. If this Pokémon finds prey it thinks it can eat, it leaps for them without any thought of how things might turn out.

tags.name: Venusaur
tags.lore: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.

tags.name: Vibrava
tags.lore: To help make its wings grow, it dissolves quantities of prey in its digestive juices and guzzles them down every day.

tags.name: Vikavolt
tags.lore: If it carries a Charjabug to use as a spare battery, a flying Vikavolt can rapidly fire high-powered beams of electricity.

tags.name: Walrein
tags.lore: Its thick tusks are strong enough to shatter drift ice. They have been known to break, but they will grow back by the next year. The Hisui region is well known for these broken tusks.

tags.name: Weavile
tags.lore: This species corners prey as a pack, under the guidance of a leader. Weavile displays increased cunning, leading me to speculate that its evolution caused further brain development.

tags.name: Whirlipede
tags.lore: Whirlipede protects itself with a sturdy shell and poisonous spikes while it stores up the energy it'll need for evolution.

tags.name: Wingull
tags.lore: It soars on updrafts without flapping its wings. It makes a nest on sheer cliffs at the sea's edge.

tags.name: Woobat
tags.lore: It emits ultrasonic waves as it flutters about, searching for its prey—bug Pokémon.

tags.name: Wooloo
tags.lore: If its fleece grows too long, Wooloo won't be able to move. Cloth made with the wool of this Pokémon is surprisingly strong.

tags.name: Xerneas
tags.lore: When the horns on its head shine in seven colors, it is said to be sharing everlasting life.

tags.name: Yamper
tags.lore: This gluttonous Pokémon only assists people with their work because it wants treats. As it runs, it crackles with electricity.

tags.name: Yveltal
tags.lore: When its life comes to an end, it absorbs the life energy of every living thing and turns into a cocoon once more.

tags.name: Zacian
tags.lore: This Pokémon has slumbered for many years. Some say it's Zamazenta's elder sister—others say the two Pokémon are rivals.

tags.name: Zamazenta
tags.lore: This Pokémon slept for aeons while in the form of a statue. It was asleep for so long, people forgot that it ever existed.

tags.name: Zarude
tags.lore: Once the vines on Zarude's body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.

tags.name: Zekrom
tags.lore: Mythology tells us that if people lose the righteousness in their hearts, their kingdoms will be razed by Zekrom's lightning.

tags.name: Zeraora
tags.lore: Electricity sparks from the pads on its limbs. Wherever Zeraora runs, lightning flashes and thunder echoes.

tags.name: Zweilous
tags.lore: Their two heads will fight each other over a single piece of food. Zweilous are covered in scars even without battling others.

tags.name: Zygarde
tags.lore: Some say it can change to an even more powerful form when battling those who threaten the ecosystem.
